successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: the lower Chari-Logone and Bornu, the land of the last Rabih state

rulers.name: Rabih az-Zubayr
rulers.title: emir (elected by the Zubat al-Kubar in 1879)

ledger.x: 1890: Rabih az-Zubayr's army, a breakaway of the slave-soldiers of Zubayr Pasha, is at Dar al-Kuti.
1892: Rabih leaves Dar al-Kuti for the Chari country.
2 October 1893: Rabih takes Kukawa and rules Bornu.
c. 1894: Rabih moves his capital from Kukawa to Dikwa. The page says he "decided to transfer his capital to Dikwa" and gives no year.
1897: Bagirmi accepts a French protectorate by treaty, ending Rabih's hold on it; the French and Bagirmi forces killed him in 1900.
23 August 1901: the French kill Rabih's son Fadlallah at Gujba and the state ends.

wars.name: Rabih's conquest of Bagirmi and the Kotoko
wars.outcome: Rabih beat a joint Bagirmi-Wadai army in 1892, took the Kotoko principalities and burnt Massenya in 1893.

wars.name: Rabih's conquest of Bornu
wars.outcome: Battle of Amja (May 1893), Lekarawa (about August), Kukawa sacked; Rabih's rule dated from 2 October 1893.

wars.name: French conquest of Rabih's state (Bretonnet, Lamy and Gentil)
wars.outcome: The French column of Bretonnet was massacred at Togbao (July 1899); Lamy attacked Rabih's fortification at Lakhta near Kousséri on 22 April 1900 and Rabih was killed; Fadlallah was killed at Gujba on 23 August 1901.

certainty.note: The pages give no territory; the state was an army with garrisons (Baggara, Karnak Logone) and a capital moved from Kukawa to Dikwa.
